note: Instrument definitions and the guards enforced by data_p3_interviews.validation().

banks.name: Current workflow
spec_questions: How do you currently track startups?
Where is startup data stored?
How do you manage mentors?
How do you track incubation milestones?
How do you manage IPR?
How do you generate reports?
How do you track student innovation?
What software do you currently use?
banks.rationale: This bank is the whole point of the phase. Phase 1's P-A10 says institution-wide innovation data is consolidated by hand, but we have only ever seen the EXPORT - never the tool upstream of it. Every question here is anchored to the last completed cycle, not to the general present.

banks.name: Pain
spec_questions: What takes the most time?
What gets missed?
What information is difficult to obtain?
What do you currently do manually?
What causes reporting problems?
What information do you wish you had in one dashboard?
banks.rationale: Anchored to the last submission cycle. 'What takes the most time' is unusable without a timeframe; the reframed form asks for hours spent on the last cycle, which is answerable.

banks.name: Existing tools
spec_questions: What software do you currently pay for?
What is free?
What do you use Excel for?
What do you use WhatsApp for?
What systems does the institution already have?
banks.rationale: This is the bank that tests the 'free incumbent' assumption underpinning StartupHub's entire pricing model. Phase 0 assumes Excel / Sheets / WhatsApp are free incumbents. That is currently an ASSUMPTION, not a finding.

banks.name: Buying
spec_questions: Who approves new software?
Who controls the budget?
How long does procurement take?
What budget category would this fall under?
What would prevent you from buying it?
banks.rationale: Phase 2 proved only 4 of 25 roles hold DOCUMENTED budget authority, and none is Class A. This bank is the only way to find out whether that documentary finding matches reality - and whether the person we interview can even authorise anything.

banks.name: Value
spec_questions: If this problem disappeared tomorrow, what would that save you?
banks.rationale: todo.md is explicit that this is the right question and 'would you pay Rs 1.2 lakh' is the wrong one. It is reframed here to demand a quantity - hours, or rupees already committed - because 'it would save a lot of time' is not evidence.

role_classes.A: Mandated IIC seats - integration point, target first
role_classes.C: Off-portal gatekeepers (Purchase Cttee, IT Admin, Audit)

guards: no question may contain a hypothetical purchase-intent frame
every question must carry a bank, a probe, an evidence hook and a falsifier
every hypothesis must name a refuting observation and a real guide question
a DOCX/count may never be reported without the institution count beside it
synthetic output may never enter _exports outside _exports/synthetic/
analysis_rules: One interview is an anecdote. No code may be reported as a finding until it appears in at least 3 of 6 institutions, and the count of institutions is always printed beside it.
A claim that contradicts Phase 1 or 3A is recorded as a contradiction, never silently dropped. Phase 1's corpus is evidence too.
Paired interviews are compared on the same four questions: does the Registrar's picture match the Convener's, on venture count, on who owns the data, and on what was last paid for.
Silence is recorded. If a respondent cannot answer a question, that is a coded non-answer and counts toward the finding - an institution that cannot name its own budget head is the finding.
Quotes are verbatim only, with the recording checked. No paraphrase is ever placed in quotation marks.
Every finding states which hypotheses it confirms, refutes, or leaves open. An interview that resolves nothing is still recorded, and still costs time - say so.

ollama_rules.purpose: Validate that the interview guides are answerable and non-leading BEFORE a human is asked them. A synthetic respondent should produce an answer that is obviously synthesised and reveals nothing real.
forbidden: any synthetic text entering _exports/ (except _exports/synthetic/, which is excluded from the manifest)
any synthetic sentence being quoted as a respondent
any synthetic count entering a finding, grade, or headline
a synthetic answer being used to 'confirm' a hypothesis
recording synthetic output with a parse_status of 'parsed'
ollama_rules.instruction: Run a synthetic respondent against each guide with a deliberately wrong, inconsistent persona, to check the questions do not lead the answer. A model that answers everything smoothly means the question is leading.
